title: Managed Identity vs Service Principal
description: Choose between System-Assigned and User-Assigned Managed Identity for Azure service authentication.

data.text: You have an Azure Function that needs to access Key Vault and Azure SQL. You don't want to store credentials in code or configuration. Should you use a Service Principal or Managed Identity?
Use **Managed Identity** (System-Assigned for single-resource, User-Assigned for shared). It eliminates secrets entirely. Use **Service Principal** only for non-Azure resources or external services.

data.title: Azure CLI - Enable Managed Identity
data.code:
# Enable system-assigned managed identity on Function App
az functionapp identity assign \
  --name 'my-function-app' \
  --resource-group 'rg-functions'

# Grant Key Vault access
az keyvault set-policy \
  --name 'myKeyVault' \
  --object-id '$(az functionapp identity show --name my-function-app --resource-group rg-functions --query principalId -o tsv)' \
  --secret-permissions get list

# Azure Function code uses DefaultAzureCredential
var client = new SecretClient(new Uri("https://myKeyVault.vault.azure.net/"));
var secret = await client.GetSecretAsync("ConnectionString");

data.text: **Managed Identity** removes the need to manage credentials. Azure automatically rotates the underlying service principal. **Service Principals** require secret/certificate management, rotation, and storage.
